assumptions: U=(U1,U2), V=(Vj) mutually independent; each density <=K; rank(B)=2; D symmetric arbitrary; Q=2 U^T B V+V^T D V+alpha^T U+beta^T V+c.
steps: Given V=v, Q is a scalar linear form in U with coefficient 2Bv+alpha, plus a shift, so its conditional density cap is sqrt(e)K/|2Bv+alpha|.
Y=BV has density cap M=e K^2/sqrt(det(BB^T)) by the two-dimensional product-projection lemma.
For a two-dimensional probability density <=M: E|Y-a|^-1 = integral_0^infty P(|Y-a|<1/t)dt <= integral min(1,pi M/t^2)dt = 2 sqrt(pi M).
Therefore E|2Y+alpha|^-1 <=sqrt(pi M), and averaging conditional density gives e sqrt(pi) K^2 det(BB^T)^(-1/4).
consequence: Since det(BB^T)^(1/4)=sqrt(s1(B)s2(B))>=s2(B), the bound is also <=e sqrt(pi) K^2/s2(B).
